dimension_grades.evidence: The email contains no hedging phrases like 'no worries if not' or 'even if this isn't a fit' — it states the ask directly without downplaying it.
"I'm raising a Series A for Conduit, and I want to talk to you about leading it" and "I'd like to spend 30 minutes walking through the unit economics and our expansion data" state the ask plainly.
The sender openly states he wants Sarah to lead his Series A and explains the reason for raising — no disguising the intent as casual advice-seeking or networking.
A skeptical reader would not perceive any sentence as a disguised persuasion tactic; the flattery is tied to a concrete thesis connection and the framing is straightforward throughout.
"We didn't have a sales team for the first eleven months… drove us from first design partner to $2.8M in ARR across 40 accounts in fourteen months" places metrics in a clear time-based progression.
All traction data ($2.8M ARR, 40 accounts, fourteen months, no paid acquisition) is woven into flowing prose rather than presented as a list.
"three enterprise accounts… are pushing us into compliance and governance territory we hadn't planned to enter until next year" implies accelerating growth the reader can extrapolate forward.

"Engineers at one company would set it up, move jobs, and install it at their next company" and "The pull is accelerating faster than our current team can build for" clearly signal customer-driven demand pulling the company forward.
"Your piece in First Round Review last year argued that the best developer tools win by becoming invisible" references a specific published piece of the recipient's thinking.
The email connects Sarah's thesis about tools that "disappear into existing workflows" to Conduit's approach of hooking "into whatever orchestration teams already run."
Within the personalization passage, the sender introduces concrete metrics: "$2.8M in ARR across 40 accounts in fourteen months" and the carry-along adoption behavior as evidence.
The reference to Sarah's article flows directly into the description of Conduit's adoption dynamic and traction — it is not a separate flattery paragraph but the opening of the core argument.
The email contains no phrases like 'happy to work around your schedule' or 'whenever works for you' — it proposes specific days and asks "What works?"

"I think this is a good conversation for both of us. You've been building a thesis around infrastructure that compounds through practitioner loyalty… and we're one of the clearest examples of that thesis playing out" frames the meeting as mutually valuable.
"I'm open Tuesday or Thursday afternoon next week. What works?" proposes a concrete time window rather than leaving scheduling entirely open-ended.
"$2.8M ARR infrastructure startup" in the subject line provides a concrete traction and domain credibility signal.
"Series A conversation" in the subject line makes the purpose of the email immediately discernible.
The subject line uses standard capitalization and plain language with no ellipses, lowercase tricks, vague teasers, or 're:' faking.
